prediction.raw: 1 (YTA - You're The Asshole) I think you're in the wrong here. Although the girl was rude, your 3-year-old son did accidentally knock over her drink, causing her to lose something she paid for. As a parent, it's your responsibility to teach your child about accountability and apologizing when they've done something wrong. In this situation, a more appropriate response would have been to apologize for your son's actions, offer to replace the drink or compensate her for the loss, and use the opportunity to teach your son about taking responsibility for his mistakes. By shrugging and walking away, you not only failed to take responsibility for your son's actions but also set a bad example for him. It's understandable that you were upset by the girl's rudeness, but that doesn't justify your refusal to make things right. A more constructive approach would have been to address the girl's behavior while still taking responsibility for your son's actions. For example, you could have said, "I apologize for my son knocking over your drink. That was rude of you to speak to me like that, but I'll still offer to replace your drink or compensate you for the loss." This approach would have shown that you're willing to take responsibility while also standing up for yourself and teaching your son a valuable lesson.
